_doc: Coming down — what to do after the effects have worn off. Keyed by substance id, and ONLY by substance id: a drug with no entry here renders no section at all. There was once a per-class fallback so that any stimulant, psychedelic and so on inherited generic advice, and it put a 'Coming down' section on pages whose drug the words did not address — the stimulant text names cocaine, meth and amphetamines, and rendered on drugs that are none of them. Removed for good. The rule for this file is that an absence is better than a guess, and 'drink water and rest' padded onto every drug page would teach the reader to skip the one page where the advice is specific. Every item carries a source that was read at source. Nothing here is a product, a supplement stack or a 'detox' — where those are marketed and unevidenced, the file says so rather than staying silent, because silence is what lets the marketing stand.

ghb.lead: GHB is the depressant where the round-the-clock pattern, not the single night, is what puts people in intensive care.

items.t: Dosing through the night builds dependence in weeks
items.d: People who dose every few hours around the clock can become dependent quickly, and that withdrawal — agitation, confusion, a racing heart, delirium — is a medical emergency treated in hospital rather than at home. It is one of the few withdrawals that kills.

sources.name: Le & Richards, StatPearls — GHB toxicity
DanceSafe — GHB

items.t: Sleeping it off is not the same as being asleep
items.d: Deep GHB sedation looks like sleep and is not. Someone should be on their side, and someone should be with them.

sources.name: GHB case (PubMed 10527300)

mdma.lead: MDMA empties a serotonin supply that takes weeks to rebuild, and everything below follows from that.

items.t: Drink to thirst, not to a schedule
items.d: MDMA makes the body hold water, and drinking steadily through a night is how people end up with dangerously low blood sodium — headache, confusion, vomiting, seizures. Somebody who has been drinking a lot of water and becomes confused needs medics told exactly that, because it is treated in the opposite direction from dehydration.

sources.name: Atila et al., JAMA Netw Open 2024 — MDMA and hyponatremia
Hew-Butler et al. — exercise-associated hyponatremia consensus

items.t: Days two to four are the flat ones
items.d: The dip is not a mood you talked yourself into: serotonin is genuinely low for a few days while it rebuilds. Plan nothing that needs enthusiasm, and do not read the flatness as information about your life.

items.t: The four-to-six-week gap is the whole harm reduction plan for this drug
items.d: Spacing is what separates people who come out of a decade of MDMA fine from people who do not. Rolling again inside a month is a worse dose of a flatter drug and a longer low afterwards.

items.t: Jaw, neck and back the next day
items.d: Hours of clenching leaves real muscle soreness. Heat and rest fix it; nothing else needs to.

items.t: The after-care supplements sold for this are not established
items.d: Pre-loads, recovery packs and 5-HTP protocols are marketed on protecting your brain and curing the dip, and none of that is shown in people. Some are serotonergic themselves, which is the one direction you do not want. This app has nothing to sell you.

mda.lead: MDA is not MDMA with a different letter: it runs several hours longer and finishes more like a stimulant, which changes the whole shape of the day after.

items.t: It outlasts a night out
items.d: Eight to ten hours is normal, against four to six for MDMA. The tail lands at an hour when there is nowhere to be and nothing open, and it is a common reason people take something else to get through it.

items.t: Sleep is the hard part, and it is the thing that matters
items.d: The stimulant end of MDA keeps you awake well past the point the empathy has gone. Losing a whole night is what makes the next two days bad, more than the drug itself does.

sources.name: Van Dongen et al., Sleep 2003 — cumulative cost of sleep restriction

items.t: Same water rule as MDMA
items.d: It holds water the same way, and low blood sodium presents as headache, confusion and vomiting. Drink when thirsty rather than steadily.

sources.name: Atila et al., JAMA Netw Open 2024 — MDMA and hyponatremia
Hew-Butler et al. — exercise-associated hyponatremia consensus

items.t: The flat days come too, and later
items.d: Because the drug runs longer, the dip tends to start a day further out than people expect from MDMA.

items.t: What is sold as MDA is frequently not MDA
items.d: This is one of the most substituted names on the market, which means an unexpected comedown may be a different drug's comedown.

lsd.lead: A trip is eight to twelve hours, so the comedown is mostly about a day that has been long, and a brain that will not go to sleep on cue.

items.t: You will be awake for hours after it is over
items.d: Even once the effects have gone the residual stimulation keeps sleep away. Do not fight it with alcohol or a benzodiazepine — plan for a short night instead.

items.t: Tolerance is immediate and takes one to two weeks
items.d: Taking more the next day does almost nothing. This is a property of the receptor, not of the batch.

items.t: The afterglow is real, and so is the opposite
items.d: Some people get a settled, open few days; some get raw, tearful and thin-skinned. Both fade. Sleep, food and daylight do more than analysis.

sources.name: Zendo Project — working with difficult psychedelic experiences

items.t: If a hard one is still with you days later
items.d: Persistent fear, unreality or an inability to sleep at all after several days is worth a clinician rather than waiting it out.

sources.name: Zendo Project — working with difficult psychedelic experiences

psilocybin-mushrooms.lead: Four to six hours, so the day is usually recoverable — the aftercare is about the body and the evening, not the week.

items.t: Tiredness rather than a crash
items.d: Most people finish flat and heavy-limbed rather than low, and it lifts with one night's sleep.

items.t: Eat afterwards
items.d: Nausea early in a trip means most people have eaten nothing for many hours by the time it ends.

items.t: Tolerance lasts about a week
items.d: Taking them again in the next few days mostly wastes them.

items.t: A hard one deserves company, not analysis
items.d: Talking it through with somebody who was there beats trying to resolve it alone at 4am.

sources.name: Zendo Project — working with difficult psychedelic experiences

cocaine.lead: Cocaine leaves quickly, which is why the comedown starts while the night is still going and why the decision that matters is about the next line.

items.t: The crash arrives in hours, not days
items.d: A short half-life means the drop is sharp and early. It is the drug leaving rather than something being wrong.

items.t: Redosing is the trap this drug is built around
items.d: Each line buys less time than the one before and adds to what is owed. The crash is the same size whenever you stop.

sources.name: Cochrane — treatment for amphetamine withdrawal

items.t: Chest pain afterwards is an emergency, not a comedown
items.d: Pain, pressure or a heart that will not settle after using needs an emergency department, and telling them what you took changes the treatment.

items.t: Drinking alongside it makes a third drug
items.d: Cocaine and alcohol together form cocaethylene, which lasts longer than cocaine and puts more strain on the heart. A night of both leaves more behind than either alone.

items.t: If the low turns into thoughts of not being here
items.d: That is part of a heavy crash rather than a verdict on your life, and it lifts. Tell one person, or call or text 988.

sources.name: National Harm Reduction Coalition — responding to stimulant overamping

methamphetamine.lead: With meth the comedown is measured in days, and almost all of it is sleep debt rather than the drug itself.

items.t: The debt is the whole thing
items.d: Low mood, no energy, huge appetite and enormous sleep are the documented withdrawal picture, worst in the first days and mostly settled over a week or so. No medication shortens it.

sources.name: Srisurapanont et al., 2003 (N=168) — amphetamine withdrawal course
Cochrane — treatment for amphetamine withdrawal

items.t: Seeing or hearing things clears with sleep
items.d: Stimulant psychosis is more likely the heavier and longer the run, and sleep is the strongest single thing that resolves it. If it does not clear after sleeping, that is a reason to be seen.

sources.name: McKetin et al., JAMA Psychiatry 2013 — psychosis and methamphetamine use
Arunogiri et al., 2018 — systematic review

items.t: Somewhere to sleep matters more than anything else on this page
items.d: Days awake degrade attention as badly as being legally drunk, and it compounds for as long as it goes on.

sources.name: Van Dongen et al., Sleep 2003 — cumulative cost of sleep restriction
Dawson & Reid, Nature 1997 — sleep loss and impairment

items.t: Eat before you feel like it
items.d: Appetite comes back slowly and days without food is why the crash feels bodily. Something with salt in it goes down easier than a meal.

ketamine.lead: The two things that matter afterwards are coordination coming back later than the feeling of being sober, and what frequent use does to the bladder.

items.t: Do not drive, and do not trust your balance
items.d: Stairs, baths and roads are where this hurts people, well after the dissociation has faded.

items.t: Pain when you pee is a stop sign
items.d: Frequent use damages the bladder, and needing to go constantly with pain is how it starts. Stopping early is what keeps it from becoming permanent, and it is worth a clinician even though the conversation is awkward.

items.t: Cramps that arrive weeks in
items.d: Sharp abdominal pain in regular users is a known pattern and another reason to take a break rather than a stronger painkiller.

alcohol.lead: The hangover is not the important part of this page; the second half is.

items.t: Water and food, and nothing sold as a cure
items.d: No product shortens a hangover. Rehydration, something to eat and sleep are what there is.

items.t: The rebound night
items.d: Alcohol wrecks the second half of a night's sleep and pays it back as broken sleep and sharp anxiety the following night. It passes, and another drink makes it longer.

items.t: If you drink daily, stopping suddenly is the dangerous part
items.d: Physical dependence means abrupt stopping can cause seizures. That is a taper worked out with a clinician, not a resolution made on a bad morning.

sources.name: FDA benzodiazepine boxed warning (2020)

items.t: Months of heavy drinking, and thiamine
items.d: Sustained heavy drinking depletes thiamine, and that deficiency causes a brain injury that starts as confusion, unsteadiness and eye-movement problems. It is preventable and treatable, and worth seeing somebody about.

sources.name: MedlinePlus (NIH) — Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome

heroin.lead: Two things decide how the hours after go: whether anyone is still there, and what a break has done to your tolerance.

items.t: After naloxone, somebody stays
items.d: Naloxone wears off in roughly 30 to 90 minutes and most opioids outlast it, so someone who woke up can go back under. If breathing slows again, give another dose.

sources.name: FDA — naloxone nasal spray label

items.t: A break resets what your usual amount does
items.d: After jail, hospital, treatment or illness, what was normal before can cause an accident. Start far below it, and not alone.

items.t: Withdrawal is miserable and is not the dangerous part
items.d: What makes it dangerous is what it drives — using at an old dose, or using alone to get it over with. Buprenorphine and methadone are the treatments that work.

fentanyl.lead: Fentanyl outlasts naloxone, which is the single most important thing about the hours after.

items.t: After naloxone, somebody stays
items.d: Naloxone wears off in roughly 30 to 90 minutes and most opioids outlast it, so someone who woke up can go back under. If breathing slows again, give another dose.

sources.name: FDA — naloxone nasal spray label

items.t: A break resets what your usual amount does
items.d: After jail, hospital, treatment or illness, what was normal before can cause an accident. Start far below it, and not alone.

items.t: Withdrawal is miserable and is not the dangerous part
items.d: What makes it dangerous is what it drives — using at an old dose, or using alone to get it over with. Buprenorphine and methadone are the treatments that work.

alprazolam.lead: Xanax is short-acting, and that is exactly why the day after is sharper than with other benzodiazepines.

items.t: Rebound anxiety is the drug leaving
items.d: A short half-life means the return is abrupt and can feel worse than the anxiety it was taken for. It is temporary, and another dose restarts the cycle.

items.t: Gaps in the evening are expected
items.d: It interferes with laying down memories while it is active. Missing hours is the drug rather than a sign of something worse having happened.

items.t: Daily use changes the situation entirely
items.d: Physical dependence builds quickly, and abrupt stopping can cause seizures — the FDA's boxed warning says so plainly. Coming off means a taper with a clinician.

sources.name: FDA benzodiazepine boxed warning (2020)
